dimensions.title: Knowledge and Skill Growth
dimensions.why: The core value of a technical community is skill development.
dimensions.question: Will attendees become meaningfully better builders, engineers, researchers, or thinkers after this?
dimensions.detailWhy: This is the most important dimension for a tech community. Truly valuable events usually provide new mental models, practical lessons, real-world experience, and frontier understanding.

dimensions.title: Networking Quality
dimensions.why: High-quality connections matter more than crowd size.
dimensions.question: How likely are attendees to meet capable and aligned people?
dimensions.detailWhy: The core idea is quality over quantity: builders talking to builders.

dimensions.title: Time-to-Value Efficiency
dimensions.why: This prevents highly popular but low-density events from scoring too high.
dimensions.question: Was the value worth the time and energy invested?
dimensions.detailWhy: Many tech events have very low information density: two hours can sometimes repeat ideas people already saw online. This dimension rewards efficient use of attendee time.

dimensions.title: Organizer Credibility
dimensions.why: Organizer quality influences the overall signal.
dimensions.question: Does the organizer consistently attract high-quality people and content?
dimensions.detailWhy: Strong organizers usually bring better speakers and a stronger ecosystem, but organizer reputation should not outweigh the content itself. That is why this dimension is weighted at 15%.
